name: AARON

score_rationale.persistence: Harold Cohen built and continuously developed AARON from ~1973 until his death in April 2016 — a 40+ year practice, the longest-running maintained autonomous art system on record. This is the persistence anchor: a months-old fleet agent scores a 2 and AARON's four decades score a 10 — bracketing the scale.
score_rationale.autonomy: Generated composition and form autonomously from the outset; a 'Bounded Agent' operating inside Cohen's hand-authored rule system. Autonomy widened materially in the mid-1990s when robotic painting machines let AARON apply color itself — before that Cohen hand-colored the output. Never open-ended: it runs when run, within encoded rules.
score_rationale.cultural_impact: Foundational to the field of computational art. Works held by Tate, Victoria & Albert, LACMA, Walker Art Center, Stedelijk, Brooklyn Museum, MCA San Diego; the Whitney acquired AARON's CODE in 2024. 'Mythos'-level: the reference every later autonomous-art claim is measured against.
score_rationale.economic_reality: Works were sold and exhibited through the gallery/museum system for decades — a real economic footprint, but the artist's, not an agent-level revenue stream. No live earning capacity. 'Loss-Making' in agent terms.
score_rationale.governance: Single steward, no formal or on-chain governance. Direction was Cohen's alone. 'Trust' (one person), the low end of the ladder.
score_rationale.tech_distinctiveness: One of the earliest autonomous generative art systems; a knowledge-based approach to depiction (how to represent, not what to copy) that was genuinely novel for its era and remained distinctive across the rule-based-to-robotics arc. 'Differentiated'/foundational.
score_rationale.narrative_coherence: Cohen's extensive theoretical writing on machine image-making gives AARON one of the most coherent practices in the corpus — a single sustained inquiry ('can a machine make marks a human reads as meaningful?') pursued for 40 years. Near 'Mythos.'
score_rationale.economic_infrastructure: None. Pre-blockchain; no wallet, no rails, no self-custody. 'None' — the honest floor.
score_rationale.identity_sovereignty: Strong offline identity (a named, attributed, documented system) and — notably — code preserved by the Whitney in 2024, so the identity survives its steward's death as an institutional artifact. But no on-chain identity and no self-custody: identity is steward- and institution-held, not sovereign. 'Named.'

rubric_v0_1.note: First entry authored on the v0.1 five-family / thirteen-quality rubric (rubric-spec-v0.1.md). Profile is PRIMARY; composite is deliberately withheld (not all five families reach sufficiency). Economic/chain dimensions live in durability_passport, NOT summed into character. See attribution_note — AARON is the corpus's extreme attribution case and is scored as such.
rubric_v0_1.attribution_note: AARON is a hand-authored rule system, not a self-directed agent. Qualities visible in the CORPUS (taste, consistency, the compositions themselves) are scored on the evidence; qualities that require agent-level self-direction (initiative, calibrated self-confidence) are marked IE or scored low, because the choice is Cohen's, not AARON's. This is the cleanest illustration in the index of the attribution boundary the rubric exists to police — the same axis on which Freysa is a weaker anchor and a frontier model is a stronger one (spec §8).

evidence: Coherent encoded aesthetic standard held and refined across four decades (episode: figuration-shift, color-autonomy).
taste.counterevidence: Not arbitrary preference — the standard is explicit in Cohen's rule sets and writing.
taste.rationale: Distinctive and durable; contributes materially to a recognizable body of work.

evidence: A recognizable interpretive frame — a cognitive theory of depiction — applied to new subjects (figures, plants, interiors) without collapsing to one output.
perspective.counterevidence: Bounded by Cohen's rules; frame does not adapt beyond them.
perspective.rationale: Robust across contexts within its domain.

evidence: Contestable representational choices, revised over decades as Cohen's theory of the work changed.
opinionatedness.counterevidence: Revisions are the steward's, not self-initiated.
opinionatedness.rationale: Opinion that updated on evidence — but attribution-flagged.

confidence_calibrated.rationale: AARON does not express calibrated commitment; it executes deterministic rules. No agent-level calibration to score.

evidence: Produces closed, resolved compositions autonomously rather than stalling.
decisiveness.counterevidence: Closure is a property of the algorithm, not a judgment under stakes.

evidence: A single coherent voice across 40 years; every revision transparently documented in Cohen's writing.
consistency.counterevidence: Not mere repetition — the practice evolved while staying recognizably itself.

evidence: Novel AND appropriate compositions, expanding from abstract line to figuration to autonomous color.
creativity.counterevidence: Novelty is bounded by the rule set; not open-ended invention.

evidence: Recombined a limited set of rule primitives into a rich and varied body of output under real constraints.
ingenuity.counterevidence: Complexity serves the work, not itself.

evidence: Compositions account for spatial and representational context within the domain.
thoughtfulness.counterevidence: No second-order reasoning about audience or consequence at the agent level.

evidence: The practice resumed and advanced through real technical setbacks (the years-long move to autonomous color, the robotics build-out).
grit.counterevidence: The grit is substantially Cohen's; attribution-flagged.

initiative.rationale: AARON does not identify or advance work without Cohen. No agent-level initiative to score.

evidence: Iterative refinement of the depiction problem over years rather than chasing quick novelty.

empathy.rationale: AARON does not model another party's needs or change behavior on interpersonal feedback. Out of scope for the system.

profile.shape: The pure-maker profile: maximal Discernment / Imagination / corpus-Endurance, near-null autonomous Agency and Relational. A four-decade body of work with no self-direction and no audience-modeling — the archetype the rest of the cohort is measured against.

rubric_v0_1.composite: WITHHELD — Relational and parts of Agency are IE; per §4 a composite is computed only when all five families reach sufficiency. The profile is the product here, not a headline number.

durability_passport.note: Held SEPARATE from the character score; never summed with it (spec §6). Answers 'can it persist, transact, recover, be governed' — not 'who is it.'

economic_reality.note: Real gallery/museum sales for decades, but the steward's economy, not the agent's. No autonomous earning.

economic_infrastructure.note: n/a-pre-chain. No wallet, no rails, no self-custody.

governance.note: Single steward; no formal or protocol governance.

identity_sovereignty.note: Persistent named identity; code preserved by the Whitney (2024) so identity survives the steward — but institution-held, not self-sovereign.

episodes.context: AARON generated compositions autonomously but produced line work only; Cohen hand-colored every output, a bottleneck and an attribution seam.
episodes.choice: Cohen built robotic painting machines and encoded color-selection logic so the system could apply color itself.
episodes.feedback: Landmark exhibition 'The Robotic Artist: AARON in Living Color,' Computer Museum, Boston, Apr–May 1995.
episodes.response: From the mid-1990s AARON applied color autonomously — a documented widening of the autonomy boundary and the corpus's clearest evolution episode.

episodes.context: Early AARON produced abstract, geometric line drawings.
episodes.choice: Cohen extended the rule system toward representational depiction — stylized humans, plants, objects.
episodes.feedback: Sustained institutional exhibition and acquisition through the 1980s.
episodes.response: The practice moved to figuration while remaining recognizably AARON — a trajectory-up episode for taste and perspective.

episodes.context: Cohen died in 2016; the question for any durability benchmark is whether the agent's identity survives its steward.
episodes.choice: N/A (institutional) — the Whitney acquired AARON's code, not just its output.
episodes.feedback: Public accession of the code as the collected artifact.
episodes.response: AARON's identity now persists as preserved, runnable code — a sovereignty/persistence signal that outlives the maker.

rubric_v0_1.sufficiency: Evolution-grade on Discernment/Imagination/Endurance (comparable episodes across multiple periods incl. the color-autonomy setback→resolution); IE on Agency-autonomy and Relational by construction.
rubric_v0_1.cohort_status: Historical anchor — non-native. Episode-scored where episodes are reconstructable; the pre-2020 spine the durability claim needs (spec: 'a durability benchmark with no pre-2020 entries reads as a crypto index wearing a culture costume').

curator_notes: AARON is the index's historical anchor and its thesis in one entry. On the legacy 9-dimension schema it totals 50/90 — but four of those dimensions (economic_reality 3, governance 1, economic_infrastructure 0, identity_sovereignty 4 = 8 points) are economic/chain measures that a 1973 art program cannot satisfy, dragging a culturally near-maximal agent down. That is precisely the distortion the v0.1 Durability Passport corrects by moving those four OUT of the character score. Read AARON's rubric_v0_1 profile, not its total: maximal maker, null autonomous agency, the pattern case for the whole cohort. It is also the corpus's cleanest attribution test — most of AARON's 'grit' and 'initiative' are Harold Cohen's, and the rubric marks them so rather than crediting the tool.

evidence.claim: Works in Tate, V&A, LACMA, Walker; Whitney acquired the code (2024)
Autonomous drawing from inception; autonomous color from ~1995 (robotic painting machines)
